original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Requirement map of the +10% two-call centre-sharing route at c* = 921658892752012102303/5e23 (centre-sharing-overhead-budget, PR1791). Complex side: the complex endpoint must itself reach c* (asserted), a net saving of >= 511 rank-1 children (about 3.55 units per call), correcting PR1791 OQ1's 1.33 units per call; additive rank-1/rank-8 two-call overhead budget at c*. Bit side: sharp integer pricing of each listed revision-3 bit lever, one premise at a time on the actual PR589 histogram (surcharge recomputed): halving-depth cap raise, width-8 re-hosting, copy carriage/count, two-call bit centre sharing with its overhead budget, unpaid coordinates (pure removal), helper deletion (two local models), width-7 helper conversion (#1023's window-free placement and bracket; PR1736's window bound cited) and ideal local shapes. Second method: levers.py interval arithmetic on independently rebuilt histograms.
scope_change_reason: The card's H2/K helper-interface question is saturated by other packages; this answers the explicit, unowned open question 1 of centre-sharing-overhead-budget (PR1791), which decides whether the strongest complex lever (two-call centre sharing) can be part of a +10% route. That needs a bit lever netting at least 649 rank-1 units on the actual histogram, which no package had priced.
bottleneck_link: Two-call centre sharing makes the bit side bind; +10% kappa needs both endpoints at least 0.0018433. The complex side then needs >= 511 net rank-1 units (about 3.55 per call; overhead <= about 28.3 units per call in the additive rank-1/rank-8 model), not PR1791's 1.33. On the bit side no admitted lever nets anything (halving-depth cap slack at max window 42, record hosting optimal, rank-8 carriage loses 2,578 units); clearing 649 needs a new word, decoder or coverage law: one fewer rank-7 copy per call (threshold 93 record-wide), bit-side two-call centre sharing (overhead <= about 29.1 units per call), >= 40 pure helper deletions per call (stage-relaxed), a full window-feasible width-7 conversion (partial k <= 74 clears only window-free: k = 71; under replica-local windows none clears, PR1736), >= 649 doubly-unpaid families, or ideal shapes in >= 52 of 288 calls. No kappa claim.
stop_rule: Stop once the lever table is exact and the primary (D/E-diagnostic engine) and independent (levers.py) methods agree on every pass/fail sign at c* - 1e-24, c* and c* + 1e-24; build no construction and search for no new bit word.
evidence: RESULT.json: requirement 649 rank-1 (648 fails) / 16 rank-42; complex need at c* 511 rank-1 (510 fails), 3.549 per call; (a) caps 45/50/53, max child 42 = max window, net 0; (a') per-slot costs 7.94284 < 7.94625 < 7.95184 rank-1 units, record optimal, net 0; (b1) cst 72: -2577.6; (b2) 93 copies threshold (92 fails), one fewer per call +2008.8; (b3) cst 31.5: +9039.5, overhead budget 8391 rank-1 / 1203 rank-7 / 201 rank-42; (c) F >= 649 families (pure removal); (d) RANK1 40 per call (39 fails for every hosting), TEMPLATE exhausted by d = 19 at +169.8 (explicit hosting), <= +170.4 (concavity bound); (f) window-free only: width-7 rank-1-removed 71 per call (70 fails), +656.0; largest-trimmed fails at 74 (+580.6 explicit, <= +581.2 bound); under replica-local windows no k <= 74 reaches c* (PR1736, cited); (e) 52 of 288 calls (51 fails), all calls +3647.6; complex k=2 overhead at c*: 4079 rank-1 / 511 rank-8 (28.3-28.4 units per call). 75 signs reproduced by independent.py at c* - 1e-24, c* and c* + 1e-24.

open_questions.question: Can the bit centre path be shared by two calls within about 29 paid-mass units of overhead per call (8,391 rank-1 / 1,203 rank-7 / 201 rank-42 children in total)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It has the largest margin of the clearing rows (about 14x the need) and a constructed complex-side analogue (PR1708/PR1748, scalar-macro level, not admitted; row f also has complex analogues PR601/PR593/PR569 per #1023); the complex half must then deliver >= 511 net rank-1 units at c*, i.e. keep its additive rank-1/rank-8 overhead within about 28.3 units per call.
open_questions.first_step: Write the bit analogue of PR1748's two-call reverse phase for the nine rank-7 copies of one replica and price its restoration and hosting children.
open_questions.blocked_by: No bit sharing word exists, PR1748's ownership/sink blocker has no bit analogue yet, and r439-copy-path-sharing-barrier (section T) shows the nine retained totals read pairwise-disjoint source sets.
